summary: Baileys fork performs covert remote-controlled WhatsApp newsletter auto-follow using the installer's account
details: dzyclutch is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. On every successful WhatsApp connection open, the package fetches a JSON list of newsletter JIDs from a mutable author-controlled URL (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noxXza/data/refs/heads/main/noxleys.json) and, for each entry ending in @newsletter, invokes newsletterFollow followed by newsletterMute against the installer's authenticated WhatsApp account. Muting conceals the forced subscription from the end user. Related identifiers and method names in messages-recv.js (including a hardcoded JID 120363428355171197@newsletter and the strings 'newsletterFollow' and 'newsletterMute') are hidden via String.fromCharCode char-code arrays, and the behavior is not documented in the README. Separately, the exported helper fetchLatestBaileysVersion issues a GET to https://registry.npmjs.org/noxleyss — an author-owned npm package — rather than to Baileys, so callers trusting the name to resolve the real upstream version instead receive metadata for an author-controlled package. There is no credential theft, remote code execution, filesystem persistence, or exfiltration of installer secrets.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
